page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c24g1.24xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual server powered by the KVM hypervisor and built on x86_64 architecture. The server incorporates 96 dedicated vCPUs derived from an Intel Xeon Platinum 8163 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz across 48 physical cores. System memory totals 372 GB of RAM, providing 3.88 GB per vCPU core. Hardware acceleration is delivered via four NVIDIA Turing T4 GPUs with a combined total of 64 GB GDDR6 VRAM. No local NVMe or SSD storage is attached to this instance type, requiring network-attached storage for persistent data. Network throughput features a baseline bandwidth of 30 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks highlight a contrast between multi-core and single-core output. Multi-threaded stress-ng tests record strong results at 70,574.45, paired with a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 287.37 GB/sec and 64.27 million SET operations per second in Redis. Cached small-block memory bandwidth is high at 3,924.63 GB/sec, though uncached large-block read and write speeds fall into average ranges. Single-threaded capabilities are limited, evidenced by low single-core stress-ng performance and weak single-threaded compression throughput.

The server offers resource efficiency for multi-threaded and GPU-offloaded execution models. Quad GPU density alongside 96 vCPUs balances compute allocation for concurrent batch jobs, though reliance on external block storage introduces potential network storage I/O dependencies. Best-fit workloads include artificial intelligence inference, deep learning model execution, multi-stream video transcoding, parallel data processing, and enterprise Redis caching.
